## Purpose

[taxonAlign](https://github.com/traitecoevo/taxonAlign) is an R package that aligns lists of raw
taxon names (for example from a trait database or field survey) to one or more taxonomic reference
lists, and then updates outdated names to their currently accepted names. The Australian Faunal
Directory (AFD) is the core reference for Australian animals.

We received the AFD in two formats and wrote a separate loading function for each:

| Export | Received | File(s) | Loading function |
|---|---|---|---|
| AFD format | 7 October 2026 | `Anamalia_all_ranks.csv` (130,503 rows) | `load_AFD(path = ...)`, in this document's [appendix](#afd-format-reader) |
| NSL format | 29 September 2026 | `AFD_export_taxon_20260929.txt` (312,601 rows), `AFD_export_name_20260929.txt` (314,913 rows) | `load_NSL("animals")`, in the companion package [taxonAlign.dataprep](https://github.com/traitecoevo/taxonAlign.dataprep) |

taxonAlign now uses the NSL format. It is published in taxonAlign's provisional data
release ([`2026-10-07`](https://github.com/traitecoevo/taxonAlign.dataprep/releases/tag/2026-10-07)):
the export exactly as supplied, and the reshaped list taxonAlign matches against (the dataset
`"NSL_animals"`). The AFD-format loader is in this
document's appendix so the two formats can still be compared.

The two loaders were written independently, each applying its own rules to its own format. That lets
us compare the results as an independent check that information was carried correctly from one
format to the other (see [Cross-check](#cross-check)).

This document records:

- exactly what each loader does to the data;
- every data issue we found and how we handle it;
- the differences between the two exports;
- [possible errors in the input data](#possible-errors);
- the results of [aligning a real name list](#real-name-list) against each format;
- [GBIF names for Australian animals that are not in the AFD](#gbif-not-in-afd);
- a short list of [items for curator attention](#for-curator-attention).

All counts below come from running the loaders on the files listed above.

### What we do *not* do

The loaders only reshape the data. The only rows left out are placeholders that don't
represent a nameable taxon (see [Unplaced rows](#unplaced-rows)).

## The target format

Both loaders produce the same flat table, one row per name, with these columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `canonical_name` | The name without authorship (what names are matched against) |
| `scientific_name` | The name with authorship |
| `taxon_rank` | Rank of the name |
| `taxonomic_status` | `accepted`, or the kind of synonym/other status |
| `taxonomic_dataset` | Source label |
| `genus` | The genus the name itself sits in (`NA` above genus rank) |
| `taxon_ID` | Identifier of this name record |
| `accepted_name_usage_ID` | `taxon_ID` of the accepted name this record resolves to (itself, if accepted) |

The `accepted_name_usage_ID` column matches synonyms to their accepted names.

## The AFD format

### How it is reshaped

The AFD-format file has one row per accepted species or subspecies (126,740 species and 3,763 subspecies rows).
The higher classification sits in its own columns, and every synonym is packed into a single
semicolon-separated free-text field (`SYNONYMS`). The loader builds three kinds of rows from this:

1. **Accepted species/subspecies.** One per row: `canonical_name` from `VALID_NAME`, `scientific_name`
   from `COMPLETE_NAME`, and `CONCEPT_GUID` as the identifier. Rank is "subspecies" when
   `SUB_SPECIES` is filled, otherwise "species".
2. **Higher ranks.** One row per distinct value in each classification column, from `PHYLUM` down to
   `SUB_GENUS`. These ranks have no identifier in the AFD format, so we create one from the rank and the
   name (e.g. `genus:Agrilus`). The rank prefix matters because, under the nominotypical-subgenus
   convention, a genus and its subgenus routinely share a name. Family and higher ranks are exported in
   capitals (`BUPRESTIDAE`) while subfamily and lower are not (`Agrilinae`), so all are converted to
   sentence case.
3. **Synonyms and other combinations.** Two free-text fields are read: `SYNONYMS` (labelled
   "synonym") and `CHANGED_COMBINATION_NAMES` (other combinations of the same species name, e.g.
   `Costalynia cardinalis` under *Rissoina cardinalis*; labelled "Generic combination", as in the NSL
   format). A name listed in both fields for the same taxon is kept once. Each field is split on
   `"; "`, editorial annotations and authorship are removed from each entry to give its
   `canonical_name`, and each entry is linked to its row's `CONCEPT_GUID`. The free-text fields have
   no separator between a name and its authorship. To find where authorship begins, we use the file's
   own `AUTHOR` column as a dictionary of author strings, with a general fallback pattern for authors
   not in that list. A synonym's `genus` is taken from the synonym itself, not from the accepted
   name, since the two often differ. Its rank is taken from its number of words: three or more
   (ignoring a subgenus) is a subspecies. Where an entry is marked as a misapplied or part usage
   (`sensu`, `auct.`, `auctt.`, `auctorum`, `non`, `nec`, `(part)`, `[pars]`), the marker is removed
   from the name and recorded as its status instead: "misapplied", "pro parte synonym" or
   "pro parte misapplied". This status matters when a name leads to more than one accepted name (see
   [Names that lead to more than one accepted name](#multiple-accepted-names)).

Output: 285,062 rows (171,260 accepted at all ranks, 99,055 synonyms, 14,164 generic combinations,
31 misapplied, 26 pro parte synonyms, 1 pro parte misapplied, 525 "unplaced" names).

### Changes from the previous AFD-format file

We compared this file with the previous AFD-format file we had been using (117,471 rows):

- `FULL_NAME` has been renamed `VALID_NAME` with the same content; the loader accepts either.
- `SUBSPECIES_COUNT_IN_SPECIES`, `LAST_MODIFIED`, `ECOLOGY_DESCRIPTIORS`, `IBRA_REGIONS`,
  `IMCRA_REGIONS`, `AUS_STATES` and `DRAINAGE_BASIN_DISTRIBUTIONS` have been removed (none were
  used). `LAST_UPDATED` has been added.
- `CHANGED_COMBINATION` now uses `Yes`/`No` instead of `Y`.
- `COMPLETE_NAME` changed from `"Aaaaba fossicollis, Kerremans 1903"` to the standard
  `"Urastoma cyprinae (Graff, 1882)"` form, with changed-combination authorship in parentheses.
- Coverage now includes Chordata. The file is still Animalia only, with no protists.
- Despite the filename, there are still no separate rows for higher ranks.
- **`CONCEPT_GUID` is not stable between exports.** Only about 20% of the previous export's GUIDs
  appear in this one. We understand the AFD team is already aware of this. In practice we treat
  `CONCEPT_GUID` as an identifier within a single export, and never store it as a permanent link to
  a taxon concept across exports.

### Data issues found, and how we handle them

| Issue | Example | Extent | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| A taxon's own name repeated in its `SYNONYMS` field | `"Neppia magnibursalis Sluys & Kawakatsu, 2001"` listed as a synonym of itself | 70,795 of 175,438 synonym entries; another 1,207 differ only in how the authorship is written | Dropped |
| Citation separated from its name by `"; "` | `"…; Phalaena inquinalis; Swinhoe, 1892; …"` | 176 entries in 146 taxa | Joined back to the preceding name (`"Phalaena inquinalis Swinhoe, 1892"`). Without this, `"Swinhoe, 1892"` would become a "synonym" of its own |
| Multi-author or particle-prefixed authorship only partly in the `AUTHOR` list | `"Gymnothorax griffini Whitley & Hutchins, 1988"`, `"Platydemus manokwari de Beauchamp, 1962"` | 1,247 entries | Leftover fragments (`"Whitley &"`, `"de"`) removed |
| Control characters or tabs inside names | `"Prosocratus \t carolinae"`, `"Brancuporus<U+0012> gottwaldi"` | 5 `VALID_NAME`s, 6 `COMPLETE_NAME`s, 10 `SYNONYMS` fields | Replaced with a single space |
| Uncertainty marks | `"? Goniada peruana"`, `"Acanthoglossa? setigera"`, `"Eristalis ?aenescens"`, `"Megascolides(?) pygmaeus"`, `"Rissoa (Ceratia ?) subtruncata"` | 119 entries | Marks removed |
| `[sic]` | `"Iodis [sic] iosticta"` | 118 entries | Removed |
| Square brackets around part or all of a name | `"H[yla] jacksonii"`, `"Hyla [aurea] ulongensis"`, `"[Spongia clathrus]"` | 128 entries | Brackets removed, content kept (as the NSL format writes these names) |
| HTML tags | `"Paraponyx <i></i> pudica"`, `"Litocorsa sp. <em>arafura</em>"` | 28 entries | Tags removed |
| Quote marks around a genus or name | `"'Ochlerotatus' notoscriptus"`, `"\"Ziba\" flammea"` | 50 synonym entries and 23 `VALID_NAME`s | Removed from the name used for matching, kept in `scientific_name`. Both formats do this; apostrophes within names (`"Allotria d'arci"`) are kept |
| Quoted manuscript authors | `"Conus ponderosa 'Beck'"` | a few | Removed |
| Misapplication and part markers | `"Dendrodoris fumata auctt. non Rüppell & Leuckart, 0"`, `"Aulicus episcopalis sensu …"`, `"Chelonia depressa (part.)"`, `"Mopsea elegans [pars]"` | 11 `sensu`, 22 `auct.`/`auctt.`/`auctorum`, 7 `non`/`nec`, 30 part/pars; 9 of these markers are separated from their name by `"; "` (`"Paracharactis vestianella; auctt., ;"`) | Removed from the name and recorded as the status (see above) |
| Malformed parenthesised authorship | `"Coccus citri (, )"`, `"Goniastrea australensis (Milne Edwards, )"`, `"Armina cygnea (1876, Bergh)"`, `"Trichobilharzia parocellata (Johnston & Simpson), 1939"`, `"Anatoma turbinata (Adams"` | 38 empty, 12 with the year missing, 33 with the year outside the bracket, plus a few reversed or unclosed | Removed |
| Unbalanced brackets | `"Mangilia (Glyphostoma)) jousseaumei"`, `"Enoplometopus (Hoplometopus)) voigtmanni"` | 6 entries | Doubled closing bracket reduced to one |
| Author name beginning with a lowercase particle or connector, separated from its name | `"Tetraphleps parva; van Eecke, 1925"`, `"Theretra cinerea; Haines in Dowling & Haines, 1963"` | a few | Joined back to the preceding name |
| An entry with no genus | `"(Ciscadra) (G. Leraut, 2021)"` | 1 | Dropped |
| Trailing comma on a valid name | `"Wallagootacoris tasmaniensis,"` | 1 | Removed (see [Possible errors](#possible-errors)) |
| Placeholder rows for unassigned synonyms | `VALID_NAME = "Unplaced Synonym(s)"` | 79 rows (16 at species level, 63 at subspecies level) | See [Unplaced rows](#unplaced-rows) |
| Species awaiting generic placement | `VALID_NAME = "Unplaced vetula"`, `GENUS = "Unplaced"` | 303 rows | See [Unplaced rows](#unplaced-rows) |
| Placeholder value in a classification column | `FAMILY = "Unplaced to Family"` | 5 rows | Not turned into a family |

#### Unplaced rows {#unplaced-rows}

This export introduces two kinds of "Unplaced" row:

- **`"Unplaced Synonym(s)"`** rows hold names placed within a genus or species but not assigned to
  any taxon.
- **Species whose genus is unplaced**, e.g. `"Unplaced vetula (Meyrick, 1893)"` with the synonym
  `"Tinea vetula Meyrick, 1893"`.

Neither becomes an accepted name in taxonAlign. `"Unplaced vetula"` is not a name anyone would write,
and there is no current binomial to update an old name to. The names in their `SYNONYMS` fields
(510 in total) are kept with `taxonomic_status = "unplaced"` and point to themselves rather than to a
placeholder. A raw name like `"Tinea vetula"` is therefore still recognised as an AFD name, but is not
"updated" to something else. This matches how the NSL format labels such names (`"unplaced"`).

#### Columns not used

- **`LITERATURE_NAMES`** (5,080 entries in 3,600 rows) records how a name has been used in the
  literature: misspellings (`"Lissothrips taverni Mound & Tree, 2015 (misspelling)"`),
  misidentifications (`"Hydrophis schistosa Daudin, 1803 (misidentification, Australian records based
  on H. zweifeli …)"`), errors and informal names, as free text. It is not read yet: each entry needs
  its explanatory note separated from the name before it could be used. This information is only in
  the AFD format. About 90% of these names appear in the NSL format's name file, but only as names
  with no link to a taxon, and no NSL taxon record is marked as misapplied.
- **`COMMON_NAMES`** is not used for matching scientific names.

#### Synonyms whose authorship we could not remove cleanly

Three synonym entries keep part of their authorship because their formatting doesn't follow any
regular pattern:

- `"Culicoides alatus, 1956b Das Gupta & Ghosh, 1956"` (becomes `"Culicoides alatus, 1956b"`)
- `"Asterolecanium 1924 charmoyi Green, 1924"` (becomes `"Asterolecanium 1924 charmoyi"`)
- `"Gerloubia species 1: Lee, 1986"` (becomes `"Gerloubia species 1:"`)

### How the subgenus is written

`VALID_NAME` includes the subgenus when there is one, e.g. `"Pardalotus (Pardalotinus) striatus"`
(11,183 of 130,121 accepted species and subspecies). The NSL format's `canonical_name` never includes
it. Raw name lists may be written either way, so taxonAlign accommodates both conventions:

- **Matching** uses each name without its subgenus, so `"Pardalotus striatus"` and
  `"Pardalotus (Pardalotinus) striatus"` both match the accepted species, whichever export is used.
- **Output names include the subgenus**: it is put back once matching is finished, so the matched and
  accepted names are reported as `"Pardalotus (Pardalotinus) striatus"`.
- **Subgenus-rank output** is always written `"Genus (Subgenus)"` (e.g. `"Acanthiza (Geobasileus)"`),
  whether the raw name was written that way or as the subgenus alone.

A related issue in the `SYNONYMS` field: 3,305 entries are the taxon's own name written without its
subgenus (e.g. `"Clivina tenuis"` listed as a synonym of `"Clivina (Clivina) tenuis"`). These are
dropped, like the other self-listed entries in the table above.

## The NSL format

### How it is reshaped

The NSL format comes as two files with the same structure as the National Species List exports for
algae, bryophytes, fungi and lichens. The same function loads all five groups. The animals export is
pipe-delimited with snake_case column names, while the other groups are comma-delimited with camelCase
names; the loader reads both.

- **Taxon file.** One row per taxon record, with real synonym-to-accepted links
  (`accepted_name_usage_id`). Columns are used directly: `canonical_name`, `scientific_name`,
  `taxon_rank`, `taxonomic_status`, `dataset_name` (`"AFD"`), `taxon_id` and
  `accepted_name_usage_id`.
- **Name file.** One row per name, with no accepted-name links. Every name already in the taxon file
  (matched on `scientific_name_id`) is dropped. The remaining 6,736 names (4,866 `"included"`,
  1,870 `"unplaced"`) are added after the taxon rows, each pointing to itself. **The taxon file always
  takes priority**; the name file can only add names, never resolve one.

Output: 319,337 rows (312,601 from the taxon file plus 6,736 from the name file).

### Interpretation choices {#interpretation-choices}

These are the points where we had to interpret the NSL format. Please let us know if any of them are
wrong.

1. **Excluded, vagrant and intercepted taxa.** Records with `taxonomic_status` of
   `"vagrant species"` (281), `"excluded other"` (146) or `"excluded name"` (18) have an
   `accepted_name_usage_id` that points to their *parent* taxon, not to a synonym. For example, the
   vagrant `Pernis ptilorhynchus` points to the family Accipitridae. Read literally as a synonymy
   link, that would "update" a valid species name to a family name. We make these records point to
   themselves and keep their status, so the name is recognised and reported as e.g.
   "vagrant species" but not replaced. In the algae, fungi, lichen and bryophyte exports, "excluded"
   records already point to themselves.
2. **`generic_name` in the taxon file** holds the genus of the *accepted* name, not of the record's
   own name. For example, the synonym `Hartmannella astronyxis` has `generic_name = "Acanthamoeba"`.
   This applies to 110,053 synonym records. Since we need each name's own genus, we take it from the
   first word of `canonical_name` instead. (In the name file, `generic_name` is the name's own genus
   and is used directly.)
3. **Subgenus names** (`"Acanthiza (Geobasileus)"`) are reduced to the bare subgenus name
   (`"Geobasileus"`) with `genus = "Acanthiza"`, the form taxonAlign uses internally for subgenera.
   In the other direction, the NSL format's species and subspecies names don't include their subgenus
   (`"Pardalotus striatus"`), so we add it from the classification: the parent record of 10,274
   accepted species is a subgenus. This gives the same full name as the AFD format
   (`"Pardalotus (Pardalotinus) striatus"`). Synonym records have no parent record, so they are left as
   written. This is only done for zoological (ICZN) names.
4. **Informal ranks** (`"Higher Taxon"`, `"Cohort"`, `"Section"`, `"Generic Aggregate"`,
   `"Species Aggregate"`) are kept as ranks in their own right. No genus is assigned to them.
   `"Generic Aggregate"` names are written like `"Subtribe Clerina"`, whose first word is not a
   genus.
5. **Quote marks** around a genus or name (`"'Ochlerotatus' notoscriptus"`, used in both formats to
   flag a doubtful generic placement) are removed from `canonical_name`, as in the AFD format, and
   kept in `scientific_name`.
6. **Misapplication markers left in a few canonical names** (`"Saragus auctt. nec"`,
   `"Entomobrya clitellaria sensu"`) are read the same way as in the AFD format: removed from the
   name, and a plain "synonym" status becomes "misapplied" or "pro parte synonym". Elsewhere the NSL
   format has no misapplied status at all: of the 58 usages the AFD format marks as misapplied or part,
   50 are plain "synonym" records in the NSL format.
7. **Genus records pointing to their own nominotypical subgenus.** For 675 genera (e.g. *Acritus*,
   *Acanthiza*, *Sericornis*), the taxon file has an accepted genus record and a second, genus-rank
   record of the same name: "primary synonym" (544), "synonym" (129) or "replacement name" (2). That
   record points to the genus's own nominotypical subgenus, e.g. genus *Acritus* → subgenus
   *Acritus (Acritus)*. We take the accepted genus record as the genus and don't otherwise interpret
   these, but we don't know what they are meant to record (see
   [Items for curator attention](#for-curator-attention)).
8. **Repeated names in the taxon file.** 4,420 taxon records share a `scientific_name_id` with
   another record; usually the same name listed as a synonym under more than one taxon. All are kept.

## Cross-check between the two exports {#cross-check}

This comparison is a work in progress. Each round has turned up differences that came from how we
read one of the formats rather than from the data itself; we fix those and re-run. The figures below
are from the latest round (the fourth). We will keep iterating until every remaining difference is a
genuine difference between the two lists.

We compared every species- and subspecies-level name in the AFD format with every one in the NSL
taxon file. For each name, we took the set of accepted names it leads to (itself, if it is accepted),
ignoring how the subgenus is written. The two files are dated eight days apart (29 September and
7 October), so a small number of differences may simply be recent edits.

| | Names |
|---|---|
| Same accepted name in both formats | 236,197 |
| Same *set* of accepted names in both (the name leads to more than one accepted name) | 1,812 |
| Different accepted names (see [Possible errors](#different-accepted-names)) | 23 |
| Only in the AFD format | 1,308 |
| Only in the NSL taxon file | 2,658 |
| **Total** | **241,998** |

Every name that differs is listed in the spreadsheet `AFD_format_vs_NSL_format_differences.csv`
(4,750 names), with the reason for each. It also lists the names that lead to the same set of
accepted names in both formats where status precedence can't pick the same one in both (761 of the
1,812). For each name it gives the accepted name(s) in each format, every record linking them with its
status, and the name taxonAlign would suggest in each format, where status precedence decides.

### Names only in one format

**Only in the AFD format (1,308):**

- **Temnocephalidae: all 90 species in 13 genera, plus their synonyms (119 names), are missing from
  the NSL format.** The family itself is absent. Genera: *Achenella*, *Actinodactylella*,
  *Craspedella*, *Decadidymus*, *Diceratocephala*, *Didymorchis*, *Gelasinella*, *Heptacraspedella*,
  *Notodactylus*, *Temnohaswellia*, *Temnomonticellia*, *Temnosewellia*, *Zygopella*.
- **Tortricidae: 213 of 615 species in 31 genera, plus their synonyms (493 names), are missing.** The
  family is present, but none of these 31 genera are: *Acroceuthes*, *Acropolitis*, *Adoxophyes*,
  *Aristocosma*, *Atelodora*, *Authomaema*, *Clarana*, *Coeloptera*, *Constrictana*, *Cosmoplaca*,
  *Cryptoptila*, *Dichelopa*, *Epiphyas*, *Ericodesma*, *Euryochra*, *Glyphidoptera*, *Homona*,
  *Isochorista*, *Isodemis*, *Isotenes*, *Merophyas*, *Neocalyptis*, *Phryctora*, *Procalyptis*,
  *Rupicolana*, *Sobriana*, *Standishana*, *Tarachota*, *Technitis*, *Thrincophora*, *Xenothictis*.
- **637 names that are in the NSL name file, but with no link to a taxon**: 483 that the AFD format
  holds as "unplaced", 119 synonyms, 32 accepted species, 2 generic combinations, 1 misapplied.
- **59 names absent from the NSL format entirely** (listed below).

**Only in the NSL taxon file (2,658):**

- 2,347 are Protista, which the AFD format does not cover.
- 273 are vagrant, excluded or intercepted taxa, which the AFD format does not include.
- **38 names absent from the AFD format entirely** (listed below).

Most of the names absent from one format are present in the other in a slightly different form; the
differences are listed under [Possible errors](#possible-errors) where they look like errors.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## Names that lead to more than one accepted name {#multiple-accepted-names}

1,893 names lead to more than one accepted name in at least one format. On their own, such names are
ambiguous. To choose between them, taxonAlign ranks each record by its taxonomic status, using the
same precedence order as APCalign, extended with the AFD's own terms. It then uses the
highest-ranked one; a tie can't be resolved. The order is:

> accepted > taxonomic synonym > homotypic synonym > objective synonym > basionym > **primary synonym** >
> heterotypic synonym > **synonym** > nomenclatural synonym > **Generic combination** > replacement
> name > … > pro parte synonym > pro parte misapplied > misapplied > unplaced > excluded > … >
> included

**We would like the curators to confirm where the AFD's terms belong in this order**, in particular
"primary synonym", "synonym" and "Generic combination". 50 of the outcomes below depend only on
"synonym" ranking above "Generic combination", which is our assumption.

| Outcome | Names |
|---|---|
| The name is itself accepted, and the same name is also listed as a synonym: | 997 |
| … of its own nominotypical subspecies (e.g. *Agrilus assimilis* Hope, 1846 under *Agrilus (Agrilus) assimilis assimilis*) | 509 |
| … of another taxon, by a different author: a homonym (e.g. *Camponotus reticulatus* Roger, 1863 accepted; *C. reticulatus* Kirby, 1896 a synonym of *C. spenceri*) | 226 |
| … of another taxon, with the same authorship (e.g. *Aname maculata*, also listed under *Proshermacha maculata*) | 262 |
| Resolved by status precedence, to the same accepted name in both formats | 54 |
| Resolved in the NSL format only; a tie in the AFD format | 295 |
| Resolved in the AFD format only; a tie in the NSL format | 6 |
| Resolved in both, to different accepted names | 1 |
| **A tie in both formats: can't be resolved** | **461** |
| Leads to more than one accepted name in one format only | 79 |

For the 509 nominotypical cases, resolving to the accepted species is correct. For the 226
homonyms, a raw name without authorship can't say which is meant: we resolve it to the accepted name,
but a raw name *with* authorship is matched to the right one. The 262 names listed with the same
authorship as both accepted and a synonym of another taxon look like part (pro parte) usages, and are
as ambiguous as the ties below.

The **295 names resolved only in the NSL format** are almost all (287) cases where the NSL format
labels one record "primary synonym" and the other "synonym". The AFD format labels both "synonym",
so they can't be told apart there.

The **461 ties** are mostly names listed simply as "synonym" of two or more taxa in both formats
(e.g. *Planorbis fragilis*, under both *Gyraulus essingtonensis* and *G. gilberti*). In 51 of them
the NSL format lists the name as "primary synonym" of two different taxa, which looks inconsistent in
itself. **For these names we can't say which accepted name is meant.** We would like the curators to
look at them; a more specific status on the records would resolve them.

**Which of these remain once the AFD is only published in the NSL format:** the 295 names that are a
tie only in the AFD format are resolved by the NSL format's own statuses. The 461 ties in both formats,
plus 6 that are a tie only in the NSL format (467 in all), are ties *within* the NSL format itself, and
will remain until the records are given more specific statuses.

**How taxonAlign reports these names in the meantime.** Following APCalign's convention, it suggests
one accepted name and lists every other candidate with its status, so nothing is hidden, e.g.
`"Lygisaurus foliorum [alternative possible names: Lygisaurus aeratus (synonym)]"`. The candidates are
also given in a separate `alternative_possible_names` column. Optionally, a name whose candidates all
share one genus can be collapsed to that genus instead (`"Genus sp. [collapsed names: …]"`). Which
candidate is suggested first is decided by status precedence, and then, for a tie, by taxonAlign's
own rules (an accepted name sharing the name's epithet, then one of the same rank, then one published
no later than the name, then the oldest, then the order the source lists them in). These rules are a
stopgap, not a judgement on the taxonomy: the ties themselves are for the curators to resolve. A
name whose candidates are all the same accepted name -- the same valid name listed twice (see
[Valid names that appear twice](#possible-errors)) -- is not reported this way: it is matched to the
first record, with no alternatives listed.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## Test against a real name list {#real-name-list}

As a practical check, we aligned the 5,154 raw names from an Australian invertebrate trait database
against each format separately, and compared the names taxonAlign suggests. This list is typical of
what taxonAlign is used for: it includes misspellings, morphospecies codes (`"Acritus BF01"`,
`"Genus 1 sp.01 Corinnidae"`) and names written with and without subgenera.

**5,116 of the 5,154 names (99.3%) get the same suggested name from both formats.** The other 38
(36 distinct names) are listed below by cause. Earlier rounds of this test also turned up three problems in
taxonAlign itself, now fixed. One was a matching rule that sent every plain `"Genus sp."` to fuzzy
matching; this is why `"Limnophora sp."` used to resolve to the NSL format's infraorder *Lithophora*.

**A. A genus name that the NSL format treats as a synonym of a subgenus (10 names).** In the NSL
format, the genus *Homalictus* is a synonym of the subgenus *Lasioglossum (Homalictus)*, and
*Goniocolletes* of *Leioproctus (Goniocolletes)*. The AFD format has no genus-level synonymy at all.
taxonAlign can only infer that a genus known only from synonym names belongs with the accepted genus
its species lead to, so it gives the genus, *Lasioglossum*, not the subgenus.

| Name in the list | NSL format | AFD format |
|---|---|---|
| Goniocolletes | *Leioproctus (Goniocolletes)* | *Leioproctus* |
| Homalictus | *Lasioglossum (Homalictus)* | *Lasioglossum* |
| Homalictus (Homalictus) brisbanensis | *Lasioglossum (Homalictus)* | *Lasioglossum* |
| Homalictus (Homalictus) dampieri | *Lasioglossum (Homalictus)* | *Lasioglossum* |
| Homalictus (Homalictus) dotatus | *Lasioglossum (Homalictus)* | *Lasioglossum* |
| Homalictus (Homalictus) niveifrons | *Lasioglossum (Homalictus)* | *Lasioglossum* |
| Homalictus (Homalictus) scrupulosus | *Lasioglossum (Homalictus)* | *Lasioglossum* |
| Homalictus (Homalictus) sphecodoides | *Lasioglossum (Homalictus)* | *Lasioglossum* |
| Homalictus (Homalictus) sphecodopsis | *Lasioglossum (Homalictus)* | *Lasioglossum* |
| Homalictus (Homalictus) urbanus | *Lasioglossum (Homalictus)* | *Lasioglossum* |

**B. A genus with an explicit synonymy record in the NSL format, inferred differently from the AFD
format (3 names).** The NSL format lists *Lathridius* as a synonym of *Latridius*. It lists
*Trigona* as a synonym of the mollusc genus *Gomphina*, plus a second, "included" record; the bee
genus of that name doesn't appear. In the AFD format, both genera are known only from synonym names,
whose species lead to *Enicmus* and *Austroplebeia*.

## GBIF names not in the AFD {#gbif-not-in-afd}

We compared the GBIF backbone taxonomy for animals recorded in Australia with the NSL format. The GBIF
data (fetched in August 2026) are every taxon with GBIF occurrence records in Australia, plus its
synonyms. Because GBIF's occurrence records include fossil specimens, taxa GBIF flags as extinct (and
their synonyms) are left out: 20,244 of the 419,088 records. GBIF's flag doesn't distinguish fossils
from recent extinctions, so this also leaves out a few historically extinct species the AFD lists,
such as the thylacine. That leaves 398,844 records. A GBIF name counts as present in the AFD if the
same name appears anywhere in the NSL format (taxon or name file, any rank or status), ignoring how a
subgenus is written.

This GBIF list is also published in taxonAlign's `2026-10-07` data release (dataset `"GBIF_AU"`,
without the 47,797 records GBIF holds with no usable name, almost all of them BOLD Barcode Index
Numbers).

**152,704 GBIF records (148,196 distinct names) are not in the AFD.** The full list, with GBIF's
classification for each name, is in the file `GBIF_AU_names_not_in_AFD.csv`. Each name is placed in
one of five groups:

| Group | Records | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Synonym of a taxon the AFD has | 78,779 | GBIF lists the name as a synonym of an accepted name that is in the AFD: a synonym the AFD doesn't record |
| Synonym of a taxon the AFD doesn't have | 47,082 | Neither the name nor its accepted name is in the AFD |
| Accepted taxon not in the AFD | 21,998 | Accepted in GBIF, not in the AFD (14,527 species, 5,413 genera, 1,153 families, …) |
| Possible spelling variant of an AFD name | 4,378 | Differs from an AFD name in the same genus by one letter, or only in its ending (e.g. *Physa kreffti* / *Physa kreftii*, *Eosphora ehrenbergi* / *ehrenbergii*). Most are spelling or gender-agreement variants; a few may be different species (e.g. *Sargus rubescens* / *rufescens*) |
| Doubtful name in GBIF | 467 | GBIF itself marks the name as doubtful |

The accepted taxa not in the AFD are mostly Arthropoda (8,541), Mollusca (5,153) and Chordata (3,349).
GBIF's Australian filter is based on occurrence records, which can be misidentified or come from
non-native populations, so a GBIF taxon "recorded in Australia" isn't necessarily part of the
Australian fauna. Some fossil taxa may also remain where GBIF has no extinct flag for them.

## Possible errors in input data {#possible-errors}

These are records that look like errors in the source data rather than issues of format. We have not
changed any of them; how taxonAlign currently treats each one is noted below.

### Valid names that appear twice

Twelve valid names each appear on two separate rows of the AFD format, with different
`CONCEPT_GUID`s. **The same twelve names are also duplicated in the NSL format**, so they come from
the AFD itself rather than from the AFD-format export process. Most are Chalcidoidea described by Girault.

The pairs fall into two patterns. We have described what the data shows without trying to judge the
taxonomy, which is for the curators to resolve.

**Identical name and authorship on both rows (3 names).** These are either two records for one
species, or two different species, originally described in different genera, that are now homonyms in
the same genus.

| | (Girault, 1934) | *Rhicnopeltella gemma* Girault, 1934 | 48f1b73c-acce-44bb-8bf9-1d8623485d4d |
| *Sphegipterosemella unicolor* | (Girault, 1914) | *Pterosema unicolor* Girault, 1914 | 51bd0a57-4e8d-479e-803d-2cc0e14a10d8 |
| | Girault, 1913 | — | 74631dfb-30ac-45f8-826c-f831f34be725 |
| *Tachinaephagus australiensis* | (Girault, 1914) | *Phaenodiscus australiensis* Girault, 1914 | 1e2bbc95-68e3-4bcf-b4a3-7c2fc5573be8 |
| | (Girault, 1915) | *Phaenodiscoides australiensis* Girault, 1915 | f4ca826b-0d34-44dc-9393-2e03eb037a45 |
| *Tetrastichus kurandensis* | Girault, 1914 | — | b3e1c187-1129-4f27-9442-a663b3824490 |
| | (Girault, 1913) | *Aprostocetus kurandensis* Girault, 1913 | c705b20d-2dba-4b40-b80f-c216959404f8 |

"—" means the row's only synonym entry was the valid name itself.

**How taxonAlign treats these:** both records are kept. A raw name matching one of these names can't
be told apart by name alone, so it is matched to the first record. The original combinations listed
as synonyms (e.g. *Secodella ovativentris*) still lead to an accepted name, but where both original
combinations are identical (e.g. *Rhicnopeltella dei* Girault, 1926 and 1933), they lead to the same
first record.

### Trailing comma in a valid name

*Wallagootacoris tasmaniensis* (Miridae) is written `"tasmaniensis,"` (with a trailing comma) in the
AFD format's `SPECIES` column. The comma carries through to `VALID_NAME`
(`"Wallagootacoris tasmaniensis,"`), `COMPLETE_NAME` and `SYNONYMS`. The NSL format has the name
without the comma.

Before we removed the comma, this was the only accepted animal name that appeared to be in the NSL
format but not in the AFD format when we compared the two (see [Cross-check](#cross-check)).

**How taxonAlign treats this:** the trailing comma is removed when the AFD format is loaded.

### Names that lead to different accepted names in the two formats {#different-accepted-names}

These 23 names are present in both formats but lead to different accepted names. "(itself)" is not
shown: where a name's own name appears among its accepted names, it is accepted, or held under an
"Unplaced" row in the AFD format, or is an excluded record in the NSL format (which we read as
pointing to itself). Patterns:

- **The AFD format lists the name under its accepted taxon and also under an "Unplaced" row**
  (e.g. *Capua promiscua*, *Malachius luridicollis*, *Phalangista cookii*).
- **The NSL format also links a species name to a genus** (e.g. *Zaclys dannevigi* to
  *Prolixodens* as well as *Prolixodens dannevigi*).
- **One format lists an additional accepted name** (e.g. *Bathypallenopsis oscitans*, *Fungia
  danai*, *Turbinella ustulata*).

| Name | NSL format: accepted name(s) [status] | AFD format: accepted name(s) [status] |
|---|---|---|
| *Acanthiza pyrrhopygia* | *Hylacola pyrrhopygia pyrrhopygius* [synonym] | *Acanthiza pyrrhopygia*; *Hylacola pyrrhopygia pyrrhopygius* [synonym,unplaced] |
| *Bathypallenopsis oscitans* | *Bathypallenopsis longirostris* [Generic combination] | *Bathypallenopsis californica*; *Bathypallenopsis longirostris* [Generic combination,synonym] |
| *Capua acritodes* | *Euphona ammochroa* [synonym] | *Clarana arrythmodes*; *Euphona ammochroa* [synonym] |
| *Capua promiscua* | *Stereoloba promiscua* [primary synonym] | *Capua promiscua*; *Stereoloba promiscua* [synonym,unplaced] |
| *Cerithideopsilla cingulata* | *Pirenella rugosa* [synonym] | *Pirenella austrocingulata*; *Pirenella delicatula*; *Pirenella rugosa* [synonym] |

### Other formatting errors

In the AFD format:

- *Goniastrea australensis* (a generic combination of *Paragoniastrea australensis*) is written
  `"Goniastrea australensis (Milne Edwards, )"`, with the year missing. 11 other names have
  authorship with the year missing, and 38 have empty authorship, `"(, )"`.
- `"Dendrodoris fumata auctt. non Rüppell & Leuckart, 0"` has a year of 0.
- `"(Ciscadra) (G. Leraut, 2021)"`, a changed combination with no genus.
- `"Aedes (?subgenus near …"`, cut off.
- Brackets that don't balance: `"Mangilia (Glyphostoma)) jousseaumei"`,
  `"Enoplometopus (Hoplometopus)) voigtmanni"`, `"Aforia ((Aforia) moskalevi"`.
- `"Leptochloris [monomial]"`: a note in square brackets that the NSL format turned into a name
  (`"Leptochloris monomial"`).

In the NSL format, some `canonical_name` values still include part of the authorship or an
annotation, so they don't match the same name elsewhere:

- `"Conus complanatus Sowerby"`, `"Conus turbinatus Sowerby"`, `"Tellina hilaris Sowerby"`,
  `"Delena gloriosa Rainbow"`, `"Thynnus cathreinii Dalla"`, `"Termes lignarium de"`,
  `"Pediculus setosus von"`, `"Limopsis philippii A."`, `"Trigonia jukesii A."`,
  `"Perotrochus 'aff. teramachii Kuroda'"`, `"Palaemon sundaicus var. De Mani"`,
  `"Ophiothrix aristulata Investigatoris"`, `"Scarabaeus novae Hollandiae"`,
  `"Columbella Deshayes, 1844"`, `"Hypora, 1864"`, `"Epimeria Chevreux"`, `"Enneamera von"`,
  `"Suphalomitus van der"`, `"Cheiraster Luidiaster"`
- `"Ategumia adipalis kwangtungialis (Bocchoris aptalis)"`,
  `"Ategumia adipalis nigromarginalis (Bocchoris adipalis)"`,
  `"Pseudoceros sp. 4 of Newman & Cannon (2003)"`
- Stray brackets: `"Enoplometopus) voigtmanni"`, `"Mangilia) jousseaumei"`,
  `"Aforia ((Aforia)) moskalevi"`
- A control character: `"Mesomyzostoma lobus<U+009D>"`
- Informal group names recorded as species-level names: `"Otiocerus group"`, `"Sikiana subgroup"`,
  `"Zoraida subgroup"`, `"Genus A"`
- Two name-file records for `"Percalates colonorum"`, differing only in the spelling of the author
  (`Günther` / `Gunther`).

## Items for curator attention {#for-curator-attention}

In rough order of impact:

1. **Missing taxa in the NSL format:** all of Temnocephalidae, and 31 Tortricidae genera
   (see [Cross-check](#cross-check)).
2. **461 names are listed as synonyms of two or more taxa with no way to choose between them**, in
   both formats, and 295 more can only be resolved using the NSL format's "primary synonym" label
   (see [Names that lead to more than one accepted name](#multiple-accepted-names)). Please also
   confirm where "primary synonym", "synonym" and "Generic combination" belong in the precedence
   order.
3. **The NSL format has no misapplied status.** Usages the AFD format marks as misapplied or part
   (`sensu`, `auctt.`, `non`, `(part)`) are plain "synonym" records in the NSL format.
4. **23 names lead to different accepted names in the two formats** (see
   [Possible errors](#different-accepted-names)).
5. **Excluded/vagrant/intercepted records in the NSL format point to their parent taxon** through
   `accepted_name_usage_id`. Is this intended? It is the only place the field doesn't mean "accepted
   name of this record". We have assumed it shouldn't be read as synonymy.
6. **`CONCEPT_GUID` changes between AFD-format files** (already acknowledged).
7. **Twelve valid names appear twice**, with different `CONCEPT_GUID`s, in both formats. See
   [Possible errors in input data](#possible-errors) for the full list.
8. **Formatting errors** in both formats (see [Other formatting errors](#possible-errors) and the
   table of [data issues](#possible-errors)), including authorship left inside NSL canonical names.
9. **Each taxon's own name is repeated inside its `SYNONYMS` field** in about 70,800 cases. This is
   harmless for us since we remove them, but it is new compared with the previous AFD-format file and
   may not be intended.
10. **`generic_name` in the NSL taxon file** gives the accepted name's genus for synonym records. Is
    this the intended meaning of the column?
11. **Two species are placed in different subgenera in the two formats**: *Leioproctus ciliatus*
    (*Colletellus* in the NSL format, *Goniocolletes* in the AFD format) and *Megachile adusta*
    (*Hackeriapis* / *Austrochile*). The NSL format also lists the genus *Trigona* only as a synonym of
    the mollusc genus *Gomphina* (plus an "included" record). See
    [Test against a real name list](#real-name-list).
12. **675 genera have a second genus-rank record, of the same name, pointing to their own nominotypical
    subgenus** (e.g. genus *Acritus* as "primary synonym" of subgenus *Acritus (Acritus)*), alongside
    the accepted genus record. What are these records meant to say? As they stand, the same genus name
    is both accepted and a synonym. (See [Interpretation choices](#interpretation-choices).)

## Reproducing this

The NSL format is read by taxonAlign.dataprep's `load_NSL()`; the AFD format by `load_AFD()`, defined
in the [appendix](#afd-format-reader) below (run that chunk first).

```r
library(taxonAlign.dataprep)
library(taxonAlign)

afd_format <- load_AFD("data/AFD_2026-10-07/Anamalia_all_ranks.csv")

afd_nsl <- load_NSL("animals", path = "data/AFD_NSL_export_20260929")

# either (or both) can then be used for alignment, e.g.
create_taxonomic_update_lookup(c("Pardalotus striatus", "Tinea vetula"), afd_nsl)
```

## Appendix: the AFD-format reader {#afd-format-reader}

```r
# The AFD-format reader. It was an exported function, load_AFD(), until the AFD's NSL format was
# released (2026-10-22); it's kept here, rather than in the package, so this comparison can still be
# rerun. A few helpers it shares with load_NSL() come from the package itself.
extract_genus <- taxonAlign.dataprep:::extract_genus
strip_name_quotes <- taxonAlign.dataprep:::strip_name_quotes
strip_afd_usage_markers <- taxonAlign.dataprep:::strip_afd_usage_markers
afd_usage_status <- taxonAlign.dataprep:::afd_usage_status

# Removes a bracketed subgenus from a species-level name: "Pardalotus (Pardalotinus) striatus" ->
# "Pardalotus striatus" (the same rule as taxonAlign's own strip_subgenus_from_name()).
strip_subgenus_from_name <- function(x) {
  stringr::str_replace(x, "^(\\S+) \\([^()]+\\) (\\S.*)$", "\\1 \\2")
}

# Reshapes the raw AFD CSV export (one row per species/subspecies, every higher rank spread across its
# own ALL-CAPS column, synonyms embedded as a single free-text semicolon-joined field mixing name +
# author + year) into taxonAlign's flat schema. Ports the *approach* of
# ausinvertraits.addons/scripts/02_AFD_checklist_clean.R (the current, canonical version of that
# repo's AFD-cleaning script), reimplemented directly against taxonAlign's target schema rather than
# translated line-by-line. Deliberately does not replicate that repo's AusInvertTraits-specific
# GRIIS/WoRMS invasive-and-marine-species filtering or "improper name" removal -- those are curation
# decisions about *which* taxa to include, not part of reshaping the data into taxonAlign's format.
#
# The reshaped result (which expands AFD's ~117k raw rows into several hundred thousand output rows,
# once every higher rank and every synonym gets its own row) is cached as a single .rds, keyed by the
# source file's own size/mtime rather than a time-based freshness window -- so swapping in an updated
# AFD.csv is picked up automatically, without the user needing to remember `refresh_cache = TRUE`.

# Load the Australian Faunal Directory (AFD format)
#
# Reads the Australian Faunal Directory's own CSV export (the "AFD format": one row per species or
# subspecies, each higher rank in its own column, synonyms written into one free-text field) and
# reshapes it into taxonAlign's reference format, ready for taxonAlign::prepare_taxonomic_resources().
# Both the original export (`FULL_NAME` column) and the 2026 export (`VALID_NAME` column) are read.
#
# Each species/subspecies becomes an accepted row, every distinct higher-rank value (subgenus to
# phylum) its own accepted row, and every entry in `SYNONYMS` and `CHANGED_COMBINATION_NAMES` a
# synonym row pointing at its accepted name, with authorship stripped. See
# `vignettes/AFD-data-processing.qmd` for every transformation, with counts.
#
# The AFD's other export, in the National Species List format, is read by load_NSL() (`taxon_group
# = "animals"`).
#
# @param path Path to the AFD CSV export.
# @param refresh_cache Logical; if `TRUE`, re-reshapes the file even if a cached copy exists. Defaults
#  to `FALSE`. The cache is keyed by the file's size and modification time, so a changed file is
#  picked up automatically.
# @param cache_dir Directory the reshaped result is cached in. Defaults to
#  `tools::R_user_dir("taxonAlign", "cache")`.
# @param quiet Logical; suppress progress messages. Defaults to `FALSE`.
#
# @return A tibble in taxonAlign's reference format (see taxonAlign::taxonomic_reference_schema()).
#
load_AFD <- function(path, refresh_cache = FALSE, cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("taxonAlign", "cache"),
                     quiet = FALSE) {

  if (missing(path) || length(path) != 1 || !file.exists(path)) {
    if (missing(path)) path <- ""
    stop(
      "Couldn't find the AFD reference file", if (nzchar(path)) paste0(" at \"", path, "\"") else "",
      ". Pass `path` to point at your copy of the raw AFD export.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (!dir.exists(cache_dir)) dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  file_info <- file.info(path)
  cache_key <- paste0(round(as.numeric(file_info$size)), "_", round(as.numeric(file_info$mtime)))
  cache_file <- file.path(cache_dir, paste0("AFD_", cache_key, ".rds"))

  if (!refresh_cache && file.exists(cache_file)) {
    if (!quiet) message("Using cached AFD reference (reshaped from \"", path, "\").")
    return(readRDS(cache_file))
  }

  if (!quiet) message("Reading and reshaping the AFD reference from \"", path, "\"...")

  # every column forced to character on the way in -- several (SUB_GENUS, SUB_SPECIES, and a handful
  # of the free-text/logical-looking columns this function doesn't use) are sparsely populated enough
  # that readr's sample-based type-guessing can mis-infer them as logical, which would break every
  # string operation below the moment a real value showed up
  afd <- readr::read_csv(
    path, col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()), progress = FALSE
  )
  # AFD's 2026 CSV export renamed FULL_NAME to VALID_NAME (same content: the bare canonical name);
  # every other column this function reads is unchanged between the two export versions, so the old
  # and new files share one code path
  if (!"FULL_NAME" %in% names(afd) && "VALID_NAME" %in% names(afd)) {
    afd <- dplyr::rename(afd, FULL_NAME = VALID_NAME)
  }
  missing_cols <- setdiff(
    c("FULL_NAME", "COMPLETE_NAME", "GENUS", "SUB_GENUS", "SUB_SPECIES", "AUTHOR", "SYNONYMS", "CONCEPT_GUID"),
    names(afd)
  )
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop(
      "The AFD file at \"", path, "\" is missing expected column(s): ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
      ". Is it an AFD CSV export?", call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  # a handful of names in the 2026 export carry stray control characters/tabs (e.g. "evanialis\u0010",
  # "Prosocratus \t carolinae") that would otherwise never exact-match a clean query
  name_cols <- intersect(c("FULL_NAME", "COMPLETE_NAME", "GENUS", "SUB_GENUS", "SPECIES", "SUB_SPECIES", "SYNONYMS", "CHANGED_COMBINATION_NAMES"), names(afd))
  afd[name_cols] <- lapply(afd[name_cols], function(x) stringr::str_squish(gsub("[[:cntrl:]]", " ", x)))
  # quote marks flagging a doubtful generic placement ("'Ochlerotatus' quasirubithorax") are kept in
  # COMPLETE_NAME but not in the name matched against -- the same treatment synonyms get
  afd$FULL_NAME <- strip_name_quotes(afd$FULL_NAME)
  # and trailing punctuation left on a name ("Wallagootacoris tasmaniensis,")
  afd$FULL_NAME <- stringr::str_remove(afd$FULL_NAME, "[,;]+$")

  # the 2026 export adds two kinds of "Unplaced" row, both flagged here:
  #  - "Unplaced Synonym(s)" holders (SPECIES or SUB_SPECIES = "Unplaced", 79 rows): names placed within
  #    a genus/species but not assigned to any taxon -- not a real taxon at all
  #  - species whose genus is unplaced (GENUS = "Unplaced", VALID_NAME e.g. "Unplaced vetula", 303
  #    rows): a real species, but "Unplaced vetula" isn't a name anyone would write or that could be
  #    usefully matched, and there's no current binomial to update anything to
  # Neither becomes an accepted row. Their SYNONYMS (for the second kind, almost always the original
  # combination, e.g. "Tinea vetula Meyrick, 1893") are kept (see afd_synonym_rows()) as
  # self-referential "unplaced" names, mirroring the NSL export's own "unplaced" status
  afd$UNPLACED <- grepl("^Unplaced", afd$FULL_NAME) | afd$SPECIES %in% "Unplaced" | afd$SUB_SPECIES %in% "Unplaced"

  accepted <- afd_accepted_rows(afd[!afd$UNPLACED, ])
  higher_ranks <- afd_higher_rank_rows(afd)
  # SYNONYMS holds synonyms proper; CHANGED_COMBINATION_NAMES holds other combinations of the same
  # species name (e.g. "Costalynia cardinalis" under accepted "Rissoina cardinalis"), not repeated in
  # SYNONYMS -- ~15k entries in the 2026 export. Labelled "Generic combination", matching the AFD's own
  # NSL export's status for the same records. A name listed in both columns for the same taxon is kept
  # once, as a synonym.
  synonyms <- afd_synonym_rows(afd)
  if ("CHANGED_COMBINATION_NAMES" %in% names(afd)) {
    combinations <- afd_synonym_rows(afd, "CHANGED_COMBINATION_NAMES", "Generic combination", "_comb")
    synonyms <- dplyr::bind_rows(synonyms, combinations) |>
      dplyr::distinct(canonical_name, accepted_name_usage_ID, .keep_all = TRUE)
  }

  reshaped <- dplyr::bind_rows(accepted, higher_ranks, synonyms)

  saveRDS(reshaped, cache_file)
  reshaped
}

# Species/subspecies rows -- one row per raw AFD row, `taxon_rank` derived from whether SUB_SPECIES is
# filled. `taxon_ID`/`accepted_name_usage_ID` are both AFD's own stable CONCEPT_GUID (self-referential,
# matching the accepted-row convention prepare_taxonomic_resources() requires).
afd_accepted_rows <- function(afd) {
  afd |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      canonical_name = FULL_NAME,
      scientific_name = COMPLETE_NAME,
      taxon_rank = ifelse(is.na(SUB_SPECIES) | SUB_SPECIES == "", "species", "subspecies"),
      taxonomic_status = "accepted",
      taxonomic_dataset = "AFD",
      genus = GENUS,
      taxon_ID = CONCEPT_GUID,
      accepted_name_usage_ID = CONCEPT_GUID
    )
}

# One synthesised row per distinct, non-blank value of every higher-rank column AFD provides (subgenus
# through phylum). None of these ranks have a natural stable ID in the raw data (AFD's CONCEPT_GUID
# only exists at species/subspecies level), so `taxon_ID`/`accepted_name_usage_ID` fall back to the
# rank's own name, namespaced with the rank itself (`"<rank>:<name>"`), not the bare name alone -- a
# bare-name fallback would collide across ranks whenever the same string is used at two different
# ranks, which for genus/subgenus isn't a rare coincidence but the norm (every genus split into
# subgenera has a *nominotypical* subgenus sharing the genus's own name). Without namespacing,
# `update_taxa()`'s `taxon_ID`-keyed lookup (`match()`, first-hit semantics) would silently resolve a
# subgenus-rank match to whichever colliding row happens to bind first (genus, since it's listed before
# subgenus in `resources`) -- collapsing a correct subgenus-rank resolution down to genus rank.
#
# `genus` is only populated for genus- and subgenus-rank rows (subgenus rows need their owning genus so
# prepare_taxonomic_resources() can build the bracketed `Genus (Subgenus)` convention automatically) --
# every other higher rank leaves `genus` NA, matching how e.g. family-rank rows work elsewhere in
# taxonAlign (GBIF/APC alike).
afd_higher_rank_rows <- function(afd) {
  # broadest-to-narrowest order isn't load-bearing here (each rank's rows are independent), but keeping
  # it makes the source easier to scan against AFD's own column order
  plain_ranks <- c(
    PHYLUM = "phylum", SUBPHYLUM = "subphylum", SUPERCLASS = "superclass", CLASS = "class",
    SUBCLASS = "subclass", SUPERORDER = "superorder", ORDER = "order", SUBORDER = "suborder",
    SUPERFAMILY = "superfamily", FAMILY = "family", SUBFAMILY = "subfamily", SUPERTRIBE = "supertribe",
    TRIBE = "tribe", SUBTRIBE = "subtribe"
  )

  plain_rank_rows <- purrr::imap(plain_ranks, function(rank_label, column) {
    values <- afd[[column]]
    # the 2026 export uses "Unplaced"/"Unplaced to Family"/"Incertae sedis" as placeholders in the
    # hierarchy columns
    # for a taxon not yet assigned at that rank -- not a real taxon name, so never a row of its own
    values <- values[!is.na(values) & values != "" & !grepl("^(Unplaced|Incertae sedis)", values, ignore.case = TRUE)]
    # AFD's own export renders family-and-above ranks (family, superfamily, order, ..., phylum)
    # ALL CAPS ("BUPRESTIDAE") but subfamily-and-below (subfamily, tribe, subtribe) in normal title
    # case ("Agrilinae") -- inconsistent within the same file. Normalising every rank here to
    # sentence case regardless is harmless on the already-correctly-cased ones and fixes the
    # ALL-CAPS ones, which would otherwise never exact-match a normally-cased input name.
    values <- unique(stringr::str_to_sentence(values))
    if (length(values) == 0) return(NULL)
    ids <- paste0(rank_label, ":", values)
    dplyr::tibble(
      canonical_name = values, scientific_name = values, taxon_rank = rank_label,
      taxonomic_status = "accepted", taxonomic_dataset = "AFD", genus = NA_character_,
      taxon_ID = ids, accepted_name_usage_ID = ids
    )
  })

  genus_rows <- afd |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(GENUS) & GENUS != "" & !grepl("^Unplaced", GENUS)) |>
    dplyr::distinct(GENUS) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      canonical_name = GENUS, scientific_name = GENUS, taxon_rank = "genus",
      taxonomic_status = "accepted", taxonomic_dataset = "AFD", genus = GENUS,
      taxon_ID = paste0("genus:", GENUS), accepted_name_usage_ID = paste0("genus:", GENUS)
    )

  subgenus_rows <- afd |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(SUB_GENUS) & SUB_GENUS != "" & !grepl("^Unplaced", GENUS) & !grepl("^Unplaced", SUB_GENUS)) |>
    dplyr::distinct(GENUS, SUB_GENUS) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      canonical_name = SUB_GENUS, scientific_name = SUB_GENUS, taxon_rank = "subgenus",
      taxonomic_status = "accepted", taxonomic_dataset = "AFD", genus = GENUS,
      taxon_ID = paste0("subgenus:", SUB_GENUS), accepted_name_usage_ID = paste0("subgenus:", SUB_GENUS)
    )

  dplyr::bind_rows(c(plain_rank_rows, list(genus_rows, subgenus_rows)))
}

# Synonym rows, parsed out of AFD's SYNONYMS field -- a single free-text string per accepted taxon,
# semicolon-joining every synonym as "Name [author], [year]" with no other separator between the
# taxonomic name and its authorship. Splits on "; ", drops entries identical to the taxon's own
# COMPLETE_NAME (self-referential noise present in the raw data), then strips authorship from what's
# left via strip_afd_authorship().
#
# `genus` is re-derived from each synonym's own (post-authorship-stripped) name via extract_genus() --
# not copied from the accepted row's GENUS -- since a synonym can sit under a different genus than the
# name it's now a synonym of (e.g. "Cisseis fossicollis" as a synonym of accepted "Aaaaba
# fossicollis"). `taxon_ID` is synthesised per synonym row (AFD has no ID at this level);
# `accepted_name_usage_ID` is the accepted row's own CONCEPT_GUID, pointing forward to the current name
# -- exactly what update_taxa() needs to resolve a matched synonym.
afd_synonym_rows <- function(afd, column = "SYNONYMS", status = "synonym", id_suffix = "_syn") {
  known_authors <- unique(afd$AUTHOR[!is.na(afd$AUTHOR) & afd$AUTHOR != ""])

  afd$SYNONYMS <- afd[[column]]
  has_synonyms <- afd |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(SYNONYMS) & SYNONYMS != "")
  if (nrow(has_synonyms) == 0) {
    return(has_synonyms |>
      dplyr::transmute(
        canonical_name = character(0), scientific_name = character(0), taxon_rank = character(0),
        taxonomic_status = character(0), taxonomic_dataset = character(0), genus = character(0),
        taxon_ID = character(0), accepted_name_usage_ID = character(0)
      ))
  }

  # one taxon's SYNONYMS field becomes a list of synonym strings; expand into one row per synonym via
  # base recycling (rep()/unlist()) rather than adding tidyr just for unnest()
  split_synonyms <- lapply(stringr::str_split(has_synonyms$SYNONYMS, "; "), rejoin_afd_synonym_fragments)
  n_synonyms <- lengths(split_synonyms)

  if (!"UNPLACED" %in% names(has_synonyms)) has_synonyms$UNPLACED <- FALSE
  synonym_entries <- has_synonyms[rep(seq_len(nrow(has_synonyms)), n_synonyms), c("CONCEPT_GUID", "COMPLETE_NAME", "FULL_NAME", "UNPLACED")]
  synonym_entries$synonym <- stringr::str_trim(unlist(split_synonyms))

  synonym_entries <- synonym_entries |>
    dplyr::filter(synonym != "" & synonym != COMPLETE_NAME & synonym != FULL_NAME) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      canonical_name = strip_afd_authorship(synonym, known_authors),
      taxon_ID = paste0(CONCEPT_GUID, id_suffix, dplyr::row_number())
    ) |>
    # a self-reference written with different authorship formatting than COMPLETE_NAME (or a
    # same-name homonym), or just without the accepted name's subgenus ("Clivina tenuis" listed under
    # "Clivina (Clivina) tenuis", ~3.3k in the 2026 export), would otherwise become a "synonym" of
    # itself -- adds nothing a match on the accepted row doesn't already give
    dplyr::filter(canonical_name != FULL_NAME & canonical_name != strip_subgenus_from_name(FULL_NAME)) |>
    # an entry with no genus left once cleaned (e.g. "(Ciscadra) (G. Leraut, 2021)") isn't a name
    dplyr::filter(grepl("^\\p{L}", canonical_name, perl = TRUE))

  synonym_entries |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      canonical_name = canonical_name,
      scientific_name = synonym,
      # rank from the name itself: three or more words (once any bracketed subgenus is set aside) is a
      # subspecies. Labelling a trinomial synonym "species" made prepare_taxonomic_resources() give it
      # a two-word binomial key, so e.g. the subspecies synonym "Pardalotus striatus kingi" claimed the
      # binomial "Pardalotus striatus" and plain-binomial queries resolved to the subspecies.
      taxon_rank = ifelse(
        stringr::str_count(strip_subgenus_from_name(canonical_name), "\\S+") >= 3, "subspecies", "species"
      ),
      # a name held under an "Unplaced Synonym(s)" pseudo-row has no real taxon to resolve forward to,
      # so it's self-referential, with its own status, rather than a "synonym" of the pseudo-row
      # misapplied/part usages marked in the free text get their own status (see afd_usage_status())
      taxonomic_status = ifelse(UNPLACED, "unplaced", afd_usage_status(synonym, status)),
      taxonomic_dataset = "AFD",
      genus = extract_genus(canonical_name),
      taxon_ID = taxon_ID,
      accepted_name_usage_ID = ifelse(UNPLACED, taxon_ID, CONCEPT_GUID)
    )
}

# Removes editorial annotations the AFD CSV writes into otherwise ordinary names in its SYNONYMS/
# CHANGED_COMBINATION_NAMES free text, which its NSL export has already cleaned off the same names:
# "[sic]"/"[sic!]" ("Iodis [sic] iosticta"), a leading "?"/"(?)" query mark ("? Goniada peruana"), a
# whole name in square brackets ("[Spongia clathrus]"), a quoted manuscript author at the end
# ("Conus ponderosa 'Beck'", 'Mytilus tortus "Dunker"') and stray quote marks ("Hypomecis” conspersa").
clean_afd_name_annotations <- function(x) {
  x <- stringr::str_remove_all(x, "<[^>]*>")
  x <- stringr::str_remove_all(x, stringr::regex("\\s*[\\[(]sic!?[\\])]", ignore_case = TRUE))
  x <- strip_afd_usage_markers(x)
  # uncertainty marks anywhere: "? Goniada peruana", "Acanthoglossa? setigera", "Eristalis ?aenescens",
  # "Megascolides(?) pygmaeus", "Rissoa (Ceratia ?) subtruncata", "Kimosina (? Kimosina) popularis"
  x <- stringr::str_remove_all(x, "\\(\\s*\\?\\s*\\)")
  x <- stringr::str_remove_all(x, "\\?")
  x <- stringr::str_replace_all(x, "\\(\\s+", "(")
  x <- stringr::str_replace_all(x, "\\s+\\)", ")")
  x <- stringr::str_remove_all(x, "\\(\\)")
  # a doubled closing bracket only where brackets don't balance ("Mangilia (Glyphostoma)) jousseaumei"),
  # not a genuinely nested one ("Pyramidella (Chrysallida (section Styloptygma)) typica")
  unbalanced <- stringr::str_count(x, "\\)") > stringr::str_count(x, "\\(")
  x[unbalanced] <- stringr::str_replace_all(x[unbalanced], "\\)\\)", ")")
  # authorship cut off inside square brackets ("Tinea lactella [Denis & Schiffermüller], 1775" arrives as
  # "Tinea lactella [Denis"), then square brackets around part of a name, kept as the NSL format keeps
  # them: "H[yla] jacksonii" -> "Hyla jacksonii", "[Spongia clathrus]" -> "Spongia clathrus"
  x <- stringr::str_remove(x, "\\s+\\[\\p{Lu}[^\\]]*$")
  x <- stringr::str_remove_all(x, "[\\[\\]]")
  # authorship with the year outside its bracket, "(Johnston & Simpson), 1939" -> "(Johnston & Simpson, 1939)"
  x <- stringr::str_replace(x, "\\s+\\(([^()]*)\\),\\s*(\\d{4})\\s*$", " (\\1, \\2)")
  x <- stringr::str_remove(x, "\\s+['\"\u2018\u2019\u201c\u201d][^'\"\u2018\u2019\u201c\u201d]+['\"\u2018\u2019\u201c\u201d]\\s*$")
  x <- strip_name_quotes(x)
  stringr::str_squish(x)
}

# Re-attaches an orphaned "<author>, <year>" fragment to the synonym entry before it. AFD writes a
# subsequent usage (typically a misspelling) with a "; " between the name and its citation, e.g.
# "Phalaena inquinalis; Swinhoe, 1892", so splitting the SYNONYMS field on "; " would otherwise turn
# "Swinhoe, 1892" into a bogus synonym of its own. A fragment is recognised conservatively: no word
# starting lowercase or with "(" (so no epithet), ends in a year, *and* the preceding entry has no
# year of its own -- old names with capitalised epithets ("Ixodes Moreliae Koch, 1867") fail the last
# test and are left alone. Seen ~176 times in the 2026 CSV export, 6 times in the older one.
rejoin_afd_synonym_fragments <- function(entries) {
  if (length(entries) < 2) return(entries)
  # a leading lowercase name particle ("van Eecke, 1925") is part of the author, not an epithet
  without_particle <- sub("^((van|von|de|da|di|du|der|den|del|della|la|le|ter)\\s+)+", "", entries)
  # ... and so are connectors between authors ("Haines in Dowling & Haines, 1963", "Smith et al., 1990")
  without_particle <- gsub("\\s(in|et|and|al\\.)(?=\\s)", " ", without_particle, perl = TRUE)
  is_fragment <- !grepl("(^|\\s)[a-z(]", without_particle) & grepl("\\d{4}\\)?\\s*$", entries) &
    c(FALSE, !grepl("\\d{4}", entries[-length(entries)]))
  # a misapplication marker split off the same way ("Paracharactis vestianella; auctt., ;") belongs to
  # the name before it
  is_fragment <- is_fragment | (grepl("^(auctt?\\.?|auctorum|sensu|non|nec)\\b", entries) & seq_along(entries) > 1)
  for (i in rev(which(is_fragment))) {
    entries[i - 1] <- paste(entries[i - 1], entries[i])
  }
  entries[!is_fragment]
}

# Strips a trailing "<author>, <year>" (or "<author> <year>") from a free-text synonym string, e.g.
# "Cisseis fossicollis Kerremans, 1903" -> "Cisseis fossicollis". `known_authors` is the AFD file's own
# AUTHOR column (a real, closed vocabulary of the taxonomists whose names appear in it) -- used as a
# de-facto authorship dictionary, since there's no other separator in the raw SYNONYMS field between
# the taxonomic name and its authorship. Sorted longest-first so a longer author string (e.g.
# "Kerremans & Boucher") is matched before a shorter one that happens to be its prefix (e.g.
# "Kerremans"). A generic trailing-year fallback (any capitalised author-looking token(s) before a
# 4-digit year) catches entries whose author isn't in the dictionary for some reason -- if neither
# matches, the entry is returned unchanged (including its authorship) rather than guessed at further.
strip_afd_authorship <- function(synonym_strings, known_authors) {
  synonym_strings <- clean_afd_name_annotations(synonym_strings)
  known_authors <- unique(known_authors[!is.na(known_authors) & known_authors != ""])
  known_authors <- known_authors[order(-nchar(known_authors))]
  # sequential fixed=TRUE substitutions rather than a single regex character class -- simpler and
  # avoids escaping edge cases entirely (fixed=TRUE treats both pattern and replacement as literal
  # strings, so no regex-metacharacter interplay to get wrong); backslash must be escaped first, or the
  # backslashes introduced by escaping every other character would themselves get double-escaped
  escape_regex <- function(x) {
    for (ch in c("\\", ".", "^", "$", "|", "(", ")", "[", "]", "{", "}", "*", "+", "?")) {
      x <- gsub(ch, paste0("\\", ch), x, fixed = TRUE)
    }
    x
  }

  out <- synonym_strings
  if (length(known_authors) > 0) {
    author_pattern <- paste0("(", paste(escape_regex(known_authors), collapse = "|"), ")")
    # optionally wrapped in parentheses -- a changed-combination's original authorship, e.g.
    # "Otobothrium curtum (Linton, 1909)", common in AFD's 2026 export
    dictionary_pattern <- paste0("\\s+\\(?", author_pattern, ",?\\s*\\d{4}\\)?\\s*$")
    out <- stringr::str_remove(out, dictionary_pattern)
  }

  # generic fallback for anything the dictionary pass didn't change: one or more capitalised
  # author-name tokens (optionally joined by "&"/"and"/"in"/",", optionally ending "et al."), then an
  # optional comma and a year, the whole thing optionally parenthesised
  generic_pattern <- "\\s+\\(?[A-Z][\\p{L}.\\-']*(?:,?\\s*(?:&|and|in)\\s+[A-Z][\\p{L}.\\-']*)*(?:\\s+et al\\.)?,?\\s*\\d{4}\\)?\\s*$"
  unchanged <- out == synonym_strings
  out[unchanged] <- stringr::str_remove(out[unchanged], generic_pattern)

  tidy_afd_authorship_debris(stringr::str_trim(out))
}

# Cleans up authorship fragments strip_afd_authorship()'s dictionary pass leaves behind when only the
# *last* author of a multi-author/particle-prefixed citation is in the AUTHOR dictionary -- e.g.
# "Gymnothorax griffini Whitley & Hutchins, 1988" -> "Gymnothorax griffini Whitley &", or
# "Platydemus manokwari de Beauchamp, 1962" -> "Platydemus manokwari de". Found in ~2k of ~103k
# synonyms in AFD's 2026 CSV export. Three conservative steps:
#  1. truncate at the first capitalised token following a lowercase one -- after the first (lowercase)
#     epithet, a zoological name only ever continues with lowercase epithets, "(Subgenus)" brackets or
#     lowercase rank markers, never a capitalised word; old names with a capitalised *second* word
#     ("Ixodes Moreliae") have no preceding lowercase token, so are left alone
#  2. strip a residual trailing (optionally bracketed) year plus the token before it (a lowercase-typed
#     author, e.g. "Iphiaulax morleyi froggatt, 1916")
#  3. strip trailing connectors/name particles ("&", "in", "de", "van der", "et al.", ...) and commas
tidy_afd_authorship_debris <- function(x) {
  # each step can expose debris for an earlier one (e.g. removing "Madhavi, Narasimhulu &" leaves
  # "(Bilqees, 1971)" trailing), so repeat until nothing changes
  repeat {
    tidied <- tidy_afd_authorship_debris_once(x)
    if (identical(tidied, x)) return(x)
    x <- tidied
  }
}

tidy_afd_authorship_debris_once <- function(x) {
  # malformed parenthesised authorship left at the end of a name of two or more words: empty
  # ("Coccus citri (, )"), year missing ("(Milne Edwards, )"), reversed ("(1876, Bergh)"), doubled
  # closing bracket ("(Turner, 1908))"), bracketed year ("(Guenée, [1858])") -- any trailing "(...)"
  # holding a comma, digit or capital letter, or nothing at all -- and authorship cut off before its
  # closing bracket ("Anatoma turbinata (Adams", "Chlamys challengeri (E.A")
  two_words <- "^(\\S+\\s+\\S+.*?)"
  x <- stringr::str_replace(x, paste0(two_words, "\\s*\\((?:[^()]*[,\\d\\p{Lu}][^()]*|\\s*)\\)+\\s*$"), "\\1")
  x <- stringr::str_replace(x, paste0(two_words, "\\s+\\([^()]*$"), "\\1")
  # (an author may also start "d'"/"l'", "Myllita deshayesi d'Orbigny", or follow a numbered informal
  # name, "Phyllodistomum sp. 2 Cutmore, Miller, ...")
  x <- stringr::str_remove(x, "(?<=\\s[a-z0-9][^\\s]{0,100})\\s+(?:\\p{Lu}|[dl]['\\u2019]\\p{Lu}).*$")
  x <- stringr::str_remove(x, "(\\s+[^\\s(]+,?)?\\s*\\[?\\d{4}\\]?,?\\s*$")
  particles <- "(&|and|in|e|et|et al\\.?|y|de|da|di|du|des|del|della|van|von|der|den|la|le|ter|of)"
  repeat {
    tidied <- stringr::str_remove(x, paste0("(\\s+", particles, "|\\s*[,&])\\s*$"))
    if (identical(tidied, x)) break
    x <- tidied
  }
  stringr::str_trim(x)
}
```
